items.q: Earl "Inky" Tremble, the sax alto man that had played with Sy in the Zack White orchestra and the Clarence Page orchestra with whom I had played before going to Europe.

ctx.x: The dance lasted until 2.30, and by the time we had packed up, loaded the bus and had a snack, it must have been 3.30 when we hit the roat for Indianapolis. I usually had to have a few shots under my belt before I could go to sleep, and after we got started, it was not long before I went to sleep. I can't say how long I had been sleeping when I was awaken by a strange quick movement of the bus. I had an idea that the bus driver was sleepy and decided to watch his reactions. I sat in the middle of the bus by a…

After a few more one nighters, we returned to the Apple, and April the first, we recorded again for MGM. A few days later, we went to Chicago for a week at the Regal theatre, after which we played a dance in Minneapolis with the Bazors as an added attraction and a dance in some town in Ohio. In Minneapolis, I was aurprised to see Earl "Inky" Tremble, the sax alto man that had played with Sy in the Zack White orchestra and the Clarence Page orchestra with whom I had played before going to Europe. I had last seen…

In Ohio, Frank Galbraith met some friends he had known for a long time, and as Sy didn't have any more jobs for a while, Frank stayed in this town. He was the first person that I ever knew that called everybody "Baby". If something was wrong, for example, a certain phrase in an arrangement, and Frank felt that he knew how it should go, he would say to the one that did not grasp the idea: "No Baby, it doesn't go like that."
